sentences.text:
The present application has been filed for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted by learned Sessions Judge vide order dated 28.04.2023 in Criminal Misc. Application No.157 of 2023 to the respondent no.2 - Doctor, alleging that he had terminated the pregnancy of the victim girl and has gone against the provisions of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 (for short 'MTP' Act).
2.

The anticipatory bail was granted in connection with the offence under sections 313, 376 of IPC,
Section R/CR.MA/10265/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/06/2023 3(a), 4, 5(l) and 8 of the POCSO Act and section 5 of the MTP Act registered at Viramgam Town Police Station vide C.R.
No.11192061230180/2023.
3.

It is stated by Advocate Mr.Trivedi along with Advocate Mr. Kartik V.Pandya for the applicant that the applicant, who is father of the minor victim girl, has filed complaint alleging that his Hasmukhbhai Shantilal Vyas vs State Of Gujarat on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105913180/
1 daughter had relation with accused no.1, and the respondent no.2 had operated the fetus without consent of his family members, and therefore, he was constrained to file an F.I.R. 3.1

sentences.text:
Advocate Mr.
Trivedi submitted that the medical practitioner cannot terminate the pregnancy in breach of provision of section 3 of the MTP Act.
He submits that no consent was given by the parents of the victim girl to terminate the pregnancy, and the Doctor was not authorized to terminate the pregnancy.
He submits that this very act is criminal in nature.

4. Ms. Jirga Jhaveri, learned APP, submitted that R/CR.MA/10265/2023 ORDER DATED:
20/06/2023 considering the nature and gravity of the offence no discretion may be exercised in favour of the applicant.

5. The additional affidavit of sister of the victim girl is produced on record, and according to the sister, her younger sister aged about 17 years studying in standard 12, had abdominal pain and,
therefore she and her mother had taken her to Hajari Hospital, Viramgam.
The Doctor on duty examined her and had given treatment and advised for sonography, if the pain continues.

It is stated in the affidavit that, on the next day, the victim suffered continuous pain and was taken to Ashram Sonography Center for treatment, and thereafter they had gone to Angle Hospital along with report and on examination by Doctor Nayan Patel, he found victim girl pregnant by six months, and advised termination of the pregnancy, and for that, stated that, victim was required to be hospitalized.

It is stated in the affidavit that mother specifically told the Doctor that without informing her husband i.e. father of the victim girl, and without taking R/CR.MA/10265/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/06/2023 advise and consent of the elders, she cannot permit the termination of pregnancy of the victim.
5.1 It is further stated in the affidavit that, as the victim was suffering continuous pain, she was admitted in hospital for treatment.
The allegation is that, they had admitted her not for termination of the pregnancy.

It is stated that, on that day, when the victim was on medication and suffering continuous pain, they had made complaint to the nurse for taking her for further treatment, and after an hour, Doctor Nayan Patel came with fetus and informed them that he had terminated the pregnancy.
5.2

The sister further stated in the affidavit that thereafter again the condition of the victim was very painful and, therefore, she was taken to another hospital named Muni Seva Hospital, Sanand, and on examination the concerned Doctor advised them to take her to better hospital at Ahmadabad for further treatment, and thus, R/CR.MA/10265/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/06/2023 they admitted her at Marengo CIMS Hospital, where the Doctor had found the right pyelonephritis with sepsis with retained product of conception and operated for right RGPT right double "J" stenting & D & E done on 08.04.2023 & right percutaneous nephrostomy diversion on 10.04.2023.
It is stated in the affidavit that in Marengo CIMS Hospital, Ahmedabad, Dr. Dhruva Patel had treated the victim girl and operated by removing 'J' Stent from the uterus.
6. Advocate Mr. Trivedi stated that Dr. Nayan Patel had terminated six months' pregnancy of the victim without consent, and therefore, violated section 3, 4 and 5 of the MTP Act.

Further, the affidavit states that the termination was without permission and was not with proper care and caution, as part of the fetus was not totally removed and minor victim had suffered unbearable pain.

sentences.text:
The learned Sessions Judge while granting the R/CR.MA/10265/2023 ORDER DATED:
20/06/2023

anticipatory bail had observed the facts that on 31.03.2023, the victim, her mother, her elder sister, who was nurse, by profession, visited the hospital of the applicant, as the victim girl had consumed abortion tablets.
On examination of the victim, it was found that she was in excessive bleeding.
The victim was admitted in the hospital after informing the parents and the Doctor was informed that the victim was married since last one year, and she was 19 years of age.

After demanding the marriage certificate of victim, the sister had shown photographs of victim with accused no.1, and on sonography report dated 30.03.2023, the age of the victim was shown as 19 years, and, thus, being a Doctor, the applicant had tried to save the life of the victim and in good faith admitted the victim, and on the next day, after pre-mature delivery, the victim was discharged from the hospital.
The Doctor had also stated before the Sessions Court that he has not undertaken any surgery or abortion.
This Court does not find any reason to interfere with the observations of the learned Sessions Judge in the anticipatory bail.

As per the affidavit of the sister, who herself is a nurse by profession,
she along with mother had taken the victim to Doctor, sonography was done, the victim was in continuous pain and she was admitted in the hospital, it cannot be assumed that there was no consent; and, further it was under consent or not, is a matter of fact to be decided during the course of trial; however, on the face of records, since the sister and mother of the victim girl were all throughout with victim, this Court does not find any reason to cancel the anticipatory bail.

Hence,
the present application stands rejected.
